figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Homologous gene clusters and related compounds of shuangdaolides. (A) Comparison of shuangdaolide (sdl), formicolide (fod), and
hamuramicin (ham) biosynthetic gene clusters (BGC) and their polyketide synthase (PKS) domains (KS, ketosynthase; KR, ketoreductase; DH,
dehydratase; ER, enoyl reductase; cMT, C methyltransferase; ACP, acyl carrier protein; TE, thioesterase). Domains colored gray are predicted to
be inactive. The genes with the same predicted function are marked with the same color, and gray indicates other nonhomologous genes. (B)
Structures of shuangdaolides. (C) Structures of formicolide B and hamuramicin B with similar carbon skeletons to shuangdaolides. (D) Structures
of hitachimycin and piceamycin with similar internal five-membered carbocycle moiety to shuangdaolides.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Inactivation analysis of genes in the sdl BGC. (A) LC-MS analysis of extracts of S. albus J1074 harboring sdl BGC or its mutants. (B)
Metabolites isolated from extracts of sdl mutant strains. The names of these novel compounds are derived from the inactivated genes of mutants.
For example, the product isolated from the mutant ΔsdlB/ΔsdlQ/ΔsdlR is named shuangdaolide BQR1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. In vitro Biochemical Reaction of SdlB and SdlQ. (A) LC−
MS analysis of the SdlQ-catalyzed reaction and proposed biosynthetic
pathway from 14 to 11. Compounds marked with an asterisk were
putative intermediates. (B) LC−MS analysis of the SdlB-catalyzed
reaction and proposed biosynthetic pathway from 12 to 15.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Functional Characterization of multidomain Protein SdlR.
(A) The conserved domains of SdlR: a ketosynthase (KR) domain, an
acyl carrier protein (ACP) domain, a flavoprotein monooxygenase
(FMO) domain, and a serine hydrolase (FSH1) domain. (B) LC-MS
analysis of extracts of mutant ΔsdlB/ΔsdlQ and its sdlR mutants. (C)
Feeding of compound 12 to S. albus J1074 and mutant strains ΔsdlB/
ΔsdlQ/ΔsdlK and ΔsdlK. HPLC traces with detection at 280 and 330
nm.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Timing of online epoxidation by the trans-acting SdlR. (A) Epoxidation occurs during chain elongation. The gray domains lack the
conserved catalytic residue required for the modification of the intermediates. The red-colored ACP domains are specifically recognized by the
HMGS cassette. The numbers represent the free acid form of the intermediates, while the blue markings represent the intermediates containing
epoxy group. (B) LC-MS analysis (BPC 200−500) of extracts of mutants ΔsdlB/ΔsdlQ/ΔsdlR/ΔTE (i) and ΔsdlB/ΔsdlQ/ΔTE (ii). Compounds
marked with an asterisk are predicted intermediates. (C) The key COSY and HMBC correlations of 28. (D) The high-resolution MS2 analysis for
intermediates 22*−24* and 28.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Proposed route for shuangdaolide biosynthesis. The gray domains lack the conserved catalytic residue required for modifying the
intermediates. SdlI, SdlJ, and SdlR acting in trans are shown. The subscript A or B indicates the predicted stereospecificity of KR domains. The red-
ACP domains are recognized by the HMGS cassette to introduce a β-branch. Compounds marked with * are predicted intermediates.
